lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs are losing the details that separate a contender from a crowded middle - and Saturday exposed all of them. Montreal's 4-2 victory dropped Toronto onto a two-game skid, with turnovers helping Alex Newhook score twice and Jacob Fowler turn aside 26 shots. At 8-8, 10th in the Eastern Conference with 18 points, Toronto has little room for another careless night. Worse, Morgan Rielly left after only 5:45 with a lower-body injury, a potentially serious blow to a defense already being asked to clean up too much chaos. John Tavares returned after missing nine games, but on the wing, not at center; that is a useful body back, hardly a full solution. Tonight's 7 p.m. meeting with New Jersey is the immediate test: protect the puck, stabilize the blue line and stop this slide before it becomes the season's defining habit.

the_latest.headline: Leafs fell to Canadiens 4-2
the_latest.dek: Toronto's late push erased a three-goal deficit but could not overcome Montreal's power-play response, extending the Leafs' slide to four losses in five games. At 8-8, they remain outside the Eastern Conference playoff picture with little margin for another slow start.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and Toronto's winter has no room for sentimentality. A 79-83 finish, good for second in the AL East, exposed a roster that needs more than a cosmetic tune-up - it needs sharper depth and a dependable offensive spine. The encouraging noise came from Arizona, where Aaron Parker turned a last-minute substitution into the Fall League Home Run Derby crown, punctuating the final with a 477-foot blast. That is not a solution, but it is a spark for a catching pipeline that needs one. The early work matters, too: Toronto has added international pitching, including left-hander Cheng-Hao Wu, while minor-league turnover has already begun. Now the club must decide which familiar free agents are worth bringing back and whether the bullpen's strength can buy room for a serious bat. Watch the next move: Toronto needs impact offense before camp, not another winter of hopeful auditions.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: A road trip that finished with a flourish still left Toronto with more questions than answers. The Raptors' 121-107 victory over Milwaukee on Nov. 6 rescued a 2-2 trip, but the wins came against inferior opposition, and the 5-4 club remains third in the Atlantic Division, 2.5 games back. Alijah Martin was the revelation, exploding for 27 points on 9-of-11 shooting and 6-of-7 from three in 31 bench minutes - a career night that demands more than a polite ovation. RJ Barrett matched him with 27 points, while Toronto survived without Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley. Barnes, Quickley and Nate Bittle remain day-to-day, with Kawhi Leonard out. The next test is at home against Memphis, a 6-3 team on Monday night. Watch whether Martin's audition becomes a permanent rotation job - and whether Toronto can turn flashes into a climb.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: Momentum has finally arrived in Washington, but it comes with a warning label. The Commanders' 27-10 demolition of Philadelphia - their first win in six games and a 27-point unanswered surge after a rocky opening - pushed them to 2-4-1, kept them second in the NFC East, and made this season feel less like a lost cause than a late rescue mission. The defense gets a timely boost with defensive tackle Johnny Newton activated from injured reserve, though Daron Payne's season-ending foot fracture leaves a crater inside. Charles Omenihu, fined $14,926 for a Week 8 gesture, must bring edge without surrendering control. Now comes the real test: Los Angeles brings Myles Garrett back alongside Aaron Donald, a pass-rush headache that will force Washington to choose its poison. At 1 p.m. Sunday on Fox, the Rams game will reveal whether Philadelphia was a breakthrough or merely a pleasant interruption.

article.title: Canadiens Beat Leafs 4-2 in Toronto
paragraphs: The Leafs fell 4-2 to the Canadiens on Saturday, with Alex Newhook scoring twice and Toronto goals coming from William Nylander and McKenna. Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 24 shots, and Toronto now turns to tonight's home game against the Devils at 7:00 p.m. ET on TSN. Morgan Rielly is day-to-day with a lower-body injury, while Bobrovsky is projected to face Jake Allen.

The Blue Jays have a promising offseason note: prospect Aaron Parker won the Arizona Fall League Home Run Derby after entering as the No. 7 seed. The Raptors return home Monday against Memphis at 7:30 p.m. ET after a 2-2 road trip, with Alijah Martin coming off the best game of his life against Milwaukee. The Commanders host the Rams at 1:00 p.m. ET on Fox, with Burks out because of a foot injury and Newton questionable with a pectoral issue. Parker's Fall Stars Game begins Sunday at 8:00 p.m. ET.
